$comment: The offer as data, so it can be read without parsing a web page. Every number here is measured, not estimated; `evidence` says how. Updated 2026-09-13 for 0.1.0-rc.6, after a connected play-through and the recorded demonstration.

product.name: NYR Underworld
product.category: standalone city / life / crime roleplay framework
product.$commit_note: Names the last commit that changed the files a buyer installs, on master. Documentation and spec commits after it do not move the product.

price.status: chosen by the seller on 2026-09-13; not yet live for sale
price.basis: Chosen by the seller from $49, $59 and $79 on 2026-09-13, for easier first sales as a new seller with no reviews. The comparables and fee model below are unchanged.

alternatives_considered.note: not justified by current evidence; no framework bridges and four systems are chat commands

pricing_analysis.cash_timing_warning: Tebex default settlement is about 14 days, PayPal withdrawal 1-2 working days, and a new payout method carries a five-day hold. A sale is not same-week cash.
pricing_analysis.before_selling: Tebex project review must approve a new project before it accepts payments. Test Mode can validate delivery while approval is pending.

contents.interface_note: Eight things have screens, reached from map blips, a ground marker and a press-E prompt at a shop, a bank branch or a door for sale, and keys F2 to F6. Gangs, police, fencing and vehicles are documented chat commands.

requirements.server_licence_key: required by both FiveM server builds, even on loopback
requirements.onesync: required; declared in the manifest so the server enforces it

compatibility.streamed_asset_packs: yes; maps, vehicles and clothing do not touch gameplay rules
compatibility.txadmin: yes, it is an ordinary resource
compatibility.positioning: This replaces a framework rather than sitting on one. It is for a new or rebuilt server, not for adding to an existing ESX or QBCore server.

licence.basis: Aligned with the Cfx Platform Licence Agreement (12 Jan 2026) sections 6.3-6.4, which license Marketplace Content for the servers the purchaser administers. An earlier one-server wording contradicted that and was corrected.

included: eight interface screens, with map blips, ground markers and press-E prompts
config.lua, validated before the server will start
MySQL persistence layer (driver not included; it uses the one you run)
audit-accepted.json, naming what a resource checker flags and why
not_included: custom maps, vehicles, clothing or streamed audio
an EMS role, dispatch or hospital
licences and courts (a sentence is a fine)
a graphical HUD (/nyrhud shows a one-line text status; anything more is drawn from me.status)

support.channel_status: must be a monitored channel before checkout opens
support.covers: installation and defects in the documented configuration
support.excludes: custom integration, which is a separate scope
support.basis: Tebex Creator Agreement section 4 requires monitored contact and a 72-hour response.

evidence.tests: 980 pass in a few seconds with no game and no server; the rules are plain Lua that knows nothing about FiveM
evidence.release_gate: manifest, licence file, credential scan, static check and backdoor audit, then the staged copy is booted on a real FXServer and its own playtest is run against that staged copy
evidence.gate_result: SHIPPABLE on the staged copy of 12a7fdc on both server builds, legacy FXServer and enhanced cfx-server (--seconds 60); boot and playtest both pass
proved: a real server boot of the staged folder, on both server builds
a scripted playtest through the resource's own command bus

a connected FiveM client on the enhanced server walked both player journeys with every check made and passed: the client drew a map mark for each place, the press-E prompt at a shop and at a bank branch, and F5 and F6 brought up their screens (663579b)
a joining player's body stays on the ground: it fell through the map on all three joins before a9fd79c, and after it the lowest point over 45 seconds was the ground

the status line no longer covers the press-E prompt: before a6348ee the two were drawn in the same corner; after it, a connected client shows the prompt at a shop and a bank alone in its corner and the line at top centre

an amount typed at the bank is dollars: 200 typed paid in $2.00 before b6997f4, found by a person at the bank on a connected client; it is converted to whole cents in tested code, and the bank screen in the recorded film shows $200.00 paid in
on the enhanced server, a resource folder that cannot be written refuses to start rather than lose the city
an unlimited starting-money loop (create, bank, transfer, retire) closed: reproduced before the fix, capped after
not_proved: E pressed at a marker, and the buttons on a screen (Buy, Take it, Pay in), driven by a journey; the commands behind them are proven, the presses are not
the journeys on a9fd79c itself: they were walked on 663579b, one commit before the spawn fix, which changes nothing they check
many concurrent players on one server
a sustained period against a production MySQL
the merged database store against a real MariaDB or MySQL; the transport check below predates it
anything a native decides that no journey reads back, beyond the marks, prompts, screens and positions above

live_database.method: the statements the store actually emits, captured from a real run, replayed with server-side parameter binding (PREPARE / EXECUTE ... USING)

verified.schema_valid: the CREATE TABLE is accepted as written
verified.on_duplicate_key_update: VALUES(payload) works on MariaDB; the MySQL-8-only row-alias form was deliberately avoided and that choice is now confirmed
verified.key_case_sensitivity: utf8mb4_bin confirmed by the server; 'Bob' and 'bob' are two rows, not one
verified.key_length_limit: a 191-character key is refused by the server outright, not truncated
verified.integers_round_trip: 218050 cents comes back as the integer 218050

transport.what: oxmysql 2.14.1 carrying this store's own statements inside a running FXServer
transport.stack: cfx-server build 139, oxmysql 2.14.1 built from source, MariaDB 12.3.3 on loopback
transport.method: the resource booted with `set nyr_store database`; a character was created through its own command bus; the write-behind flush was observed landing in MariaDB by querying MariaDB directly, not by trusting the resource's log
transport.round_trip: the server was stopped, the JSON `data` directory deleted outright so nothing could load from a file, and the server restarted: the city came back as `1 people` and `character.list` returned the character by name and wallet
transport.return_shapes_measured: oxmysql's untyped path returns mysql2's raw result header (a table), not a number; a failing statement throws rather than returning nil. The driver already normalised both, and `spec/sql_driver_spec.lua` now holds those measured shapes so a later tidy cannot quietly break the contract the store documents.

live_database.build: measured on master before the 2026-09-13 merge; the database store changed in that merge and has not been re-run against MariaDB since

recorded_session.what: a 73-second film driven by the rig with a real FiveM client connected to a real enhanced server: a character is made, runs to Pillbox Hill Branch by the game's route finding, opens an account and pays in $200, takes a shift from the job board, walks into Rob's Liquor, presses E at the counter, buys a bottle of water and opens their pockets
recorded_session.output: run/video/nyr-underworld-demo-short.mp4, 1920x1080, 30 fps, no audio, not in the repository
recorded_session.method: docs/store-page/film.py and film_walkin.py: the screen recorded through dxcam and ffmpeg while the dev bridge walks the body (TaskFollowNavMeshToCoord), presses E through the function the key calls, runs each button's command through the command bus, and redraws the screen from the server's answer
recorded_session.checked: every second of both source clips looked at on a contact sheet: no window but the game, no overlay
recorded_session.cut: a delivery truck knocking the body down mid-run, the walk that stuck at a wall outside the shop, and a take that caught a person's Alt-Tab window list are not in it
recorded_session.not_shown: a person's own key presses and clicks: E and the buttons are driven through the same functions, not by a keyboard
recorded_session.build: recorded on c475fac plus the filming scripts (12a7fdc is the same resource files)

outstanding: verified checkout and delivery in Test Mode
